phase3_findings.description: The diff's own statement of when an enrolled sub-key inherits the master is false against HEAD on two surfaces and self-inconsistent across the change. (a) Iteration 2 widened five schema sub-key clauses, the changeset and the external prose to 'absent OR set to JSON null', but left .prflow/config.schema.json's telemetry.enabled description ('resolve to disabled wherever their own key is absent'; 'the master can only DISABLE a mechanism whose own key is absent') and docs/internal/DEVFLOW_SYSTEM_OVERVIEW.md:1146 ('inherit it on their resolver miss path (only when their own key is absent)') at the pre-fix wording — the overview's parenthetical is an explicit exclusive, so affirmatively wrong, not merely incomplete. (b) The coupled universal 'an explicit sub-key value ALWAYS wins over the master, in both directions' is false for an explicit empty string: with telemetry.enabled false and prflow.execution_diagnostics_enabled set to "", the resolver prints false, so the explicit value did not win. Both halves verified against HEAD by direct probe and by checklist item VC-15.

phase3_findings.description: The new '#2035 collect-staged announces an unreadable config' assertion mocks unreadability with chmod 000 and carries no root / permissive-filesystem skip guard, unlike this repository's established pattern for the identical mock (lib/test/run.sh:24375-24390, :25564-25568, :26882; retrospective-lifecycle.sh:3074-3083; review-stall-backstop.sh:420-431, 580-587, 1313-1316; prompt-extension-reader.sh:78-86 all gate with an explicit skip). Under a root-run container or a filesystem that ignores mode bits — runner classes DEVFLOW_RUNNER explicitly reaches — the config stays readable, the collector's [ -e ] && [ ! -r ] arm never fires, and this assertion goes RED on an exact-floor module that must report 1053 passed, 0 failed. Introduced by iteration 2's own fix.
phase3_findings.phase_4_1_5_flag: shape 1 (advisory only) — the defect's failure mode is one the project's suite catches RED; the annotation does not change the verdict.

phase3_findings.description: The --persist push gate has no unconsulted-master announcement for an unreadable config, which is the asymmetric half of iteration 2's own fix. collect-staged-telemetry.sh now emits "config '<path>' exists but is not readable — the telemetry.enabled master switch was NOT consulted"; lib/efficiency-trace.sh's do_persist got only the python3-absent arm. Its inline predicate's bare `except Exception: sys.exit(1)` folds unreadable config, corrupt JSON and master-genuinely-on into one indistinguishable exit 1, and the caller falls through to the full persist silently. This is the louder of the two paths — do_persist commits and pushes to the long-lived prflow-telemetry orphan branch, where the collect path only stages a short-retention artifact — so an operator who set telemetry.enabled false for privacy and whose config is unreadable in the runner's uid gets a durable push with no signal.
phase3_findings.corroboration_note: prflow:requesting-code-review raised the same asymmetry at Suggestion with kind 'other'; mechanical corroboration requires an identical kind, so it is counted as single-source and flagged for extra scrutiny rather than merged.

phase3_findings.description: Iteration 2's unreadable arm covers only one of the three indeterminate shapes the original finding named. The added condition is [ -e "$_CST_CFG" ] && [ ! -r "$_CST_CFG" ], true only for the permission case; a syntactically corrupt config — trailing comma, truncated write, merge-conflict marker — is equally an unconsulted master (the predicate exits 1 for it) yet produces no announcement, and the module now positively pins that absence as intended ('#2035 AC5 collect-staged corrupt-config emits no skip breadcrumb'). Two smaller residuals in the same condition: -e is false when the config's parent directory is unsearchable, so even the permission case is only partly covered. Suggested fix: give telemetry-master-off.py a distinct exit 2 for read/parse failure and announce on that, which also removes the -e/-r heuristic and lets lib/efficiency-trace.sh reuse the same discrimination.
